newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian police say more MinFins were frozen in May.
newsitem.headline: Russian police say more MinFins were frozen in May.

text.p: A Russian police officer said on Monday that a large volume of Russian MinFin bonds may have been frozen this May in addition to the $24 million previously reported.
A police officer working on the MinFin case told Reuters he had been ordered to freeze a large amount of MinFins in May.

"In May I had a case in which an order was issued to freeze bonds... I may be wrong, but it could have been up to $100 million face value," said Mikhail Ignatyev, a detective in the investigations department of the 5th central Moscow police precinct.
Ignatyev said he could not state the exact amount of bonds involved as he did not have the file on the case to hand.
Officials at Vneshtorgbank, the main MinFin depositary, were not immediately available for comment.

MinFin bond dealers said that prices fell on Monday by around 1.5 big figures amid rumours that some banks had been advised that some of their MinFins, totalling more than $50 million face value, had been frozen.
Earlier this year the authorities froze $24.22 million of the dollar-denominated bonds, which had gone missing. Many of them were stolen in Chechnya.

Rumours about the first freeze started circulating in June, hitting prices of the paper, which is traded both in Russia and abroad. Subsequently the finance ministry said it would not service the frozen bonds.
The issue has still not been resolved.
In August banking sources said police were preparing to freeze up to another $7 million of MinFin bonds belonging to a small Russian bank and to some foreign trade organisations.
It is not clear whether this order has been issued.
Ignatyev said the order to freeze bonds which he had worked on in May had been based on claims by firms which said the bonds had been used as collateral to obtain a $10 million loan.
"I did not have MinFins from other cases. Since May there have been no other orders from us," he said.
